examples.en: Ready-made clothes are cheaper than tailored ones.

examples.ko: 저는 키가 작아서 기성복을 사면 늘 줄여야 해요.
examples.en: I'm short, so whenever I buy ready-made clothes I always have to have them shortened.
These days even ready-made clothes come in a variety of designs.

examples.ko: 기성복 매장에서 정장을 한 벌 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a suit at a ready-to-wear shop.

examples.ko: 기성복이 몸에 안 맞아서 맞춤 양복을 맞췄어요.
examples.en: Ready-made clothes didn't fit me, so I had a suit made to measure.

examples.ko: 어렸을 때는 기성복보다 어머니가 만든 옷을 많이 입었어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I wore clothes my mother made more than store-bought ones.

explain: 반대말은 '맞춤복'이나 '맞춤옷'이에요. 일상에서는 '사 입는 옷'이라고도 하고, '기성'은 '기성세대'처럼 이미 만들어져 있다는 뜻으로도 나와요.

phrases.en: I bought a suit at a ready-made clothing store.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷을 파는 가게를 말할 때 붙이는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for a store selling ready-made clothes.

phrases.example: 요즘은 사 입는 옷이 더 편해요.
phrases.en: These days store-bought clothes are more convenient.
phrases.nuance_ko: '기성복'을 쉽게 풀어 쓴 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An everyday way of saying 기성복.

phrases.en: I got a custom-made outfit for the wedding.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기성복의 반대말이에요. 몸에 맞게 따로 만든 옷이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 기성복; clothes made to fit you.

explain_en: Clothes only — off-the-rack, opposite of tailor-made (맞춤옷) Its opposite is '맞춤복' or '맞춤옷' (made-to-measure clothes). In everyday talk people also say '사 입는 옷' (clothes you buy), and '기성' also appears in words like '기성세대' (the established generation) with the sense of 'already made or established'.

examples.en: I haven't shaved, so my chin feels scratchy.

examples.ko: 이 수건은 빨래한 뒤에 좀 까슬까슬해졌어요.
examples.en: This towel got a bit rough after washing.
Dad's stubble was scratchy, so the baby cried.
Rough fabric stings when it touches my skin.
The laundry I just dried came out stiff and rough.
The soles of my feet feel gritty with sand.

explain: 수염이나 마른 천, 모래처럼 살짝 거칠어서 긁히는 듯한 촉감을 말해요. '거칠다'보다 가볍고 생생한 느낌이에요. '보들보들하다'나 '매끈하다'의 반대쪽 촉감이에요.

phrases.en: In the morning I had scratchy stubble.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수염이 막 자라 거칠게 느껴질 때 가장 잘 어울리는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The best-fitting pairing for freshly grown, rough stubble.

phrases.en: This blanket isn't scratchy, so I like it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 쓰면 촉감이 부드럽다는 뜻이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: In the negative, it means the texture is soft.

phrases.en: It's winter, so my hands are rough.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하지만 더 흔하고, 피부 같은 곳이 거칠 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning but more common, and works for rough skin too.

explain_en: Rough and bristly to the touch, like coarse fabric, stubble, or short stiff hair. It describes a slightly rough, scratchy feel such as stubble, dry fabric or sand. It feels lighter and more vivid than '거칠다'. It is the opposite kind of touch to '보들보들하다' or '매끈하다'.

t90.ax: This towel got a bit rough after washing.

examples.en: My skin is dry and rough.
In winter my lips get rough, so I put on balm.

examples.ko: 밤새 못 잤더니 얼굴이 까칠까칠해 보여요.
examples.en: I couldn't sleep all night, so my face looks haggard.
If you touch the baby with rough hands, it hurts her.

examples.ko: 이 종이는 표면이 까칠까칠해서 그림이 잘 그려져요.
examples.en: This paper has a rough surface, so drawing on it works well.
I woke up this morning and my chin feels bristly.

explain: 건조하거나 피곤해서 윤기 없이 거칠어진 피부, 입술, 종이 표면에 잘 어울려요. 줄여서 '까칠하다'라고도 하는데, '까칠하다'는 성격이 까다롭다는 뜻으로도 쓰여요. '까칠까칠하다'는 보통 촉감이나 겉모습을 말해요.

phrases.en: In dry weather, my skin feels rough.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ' 형태로 뒤의 명사를 꾸며서, 만졌을 때 거친 것을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form describes a noun that feels rough to the touch.

phrases.en: After staying up all night, my face got rough.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래는 괜찮았는데 거칠게 변했다는 뜻이에요. 변화를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means something that was fine has turned rough, so it expresses a change.

phrases.example: 이 크림을 바르면 손이 까칠까칠하지 않아요.
phrases.en: If you use this cream, your hands don't feel rough.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형이라서 거칠지 않고 괜찮다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says something is not rough.

explain_en: Dry, lusterless and rough, especially skin or hair; can also describe a worn, thin-looking face. It fits skin, lips or paper surfaces that have turned dull and rough from dryness or tiredness. People also shorten it to '까칠하다', which can additionally mean a picky personality. '까칠까칠하다' usually describes touch or appearance.

t90.ax: My skin is dry and rough.

en: to dress up; to spruce up; to decorate

examples.en: I dressed up nicely before the picnic.
Mom got nicely dressed up to go to the wedding.

examples.ko: 손님이 오기 전에 집을 새롭게 단장해요.
examples.en: I spruce up the house before guests arrive.
I got neatly groomed and went to the interview.
It takes a whole hour to get ready.
They renovated the shop and reopened it.

explain: 사람의 얼굴, 옷, 머리를 예쁘게 꾸밀 때뿐 아니라 집, 가게, 거리를 새롭게 고칠 때도 써요. '화장하다'는 얼굴에 화장하는 것만 말하지만 '단장하다'는 몸 전체와 장소까지 넓어요.

phrases.en: They renovated the street in front of city hall.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장소를 고쳐서 새로 꾸밀 때 '새롭게'와 자주 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often paired with 'newly' when a place is fixed up and redecorated.

phrases.example: 저는 약속이 있으면 예쁘게 단장하고 나가요.
phrases.en: When I have plans, I dress up nicely and go out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 꾸민 뒤에 다음 행동을 이어서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to link getting dressed up with the next action.
phrases.en_equiv: get dressed up and go out

phrases.en: We spruced up the shop neatly and opened.
phrases.nuance_ko: '말끔히'는 깨끗하고 단정하게 꾸몄다는 느낌을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '말끔히' adds a feeling of being neat and clean.

explain_en: Making oneself or a place neat and pretty, slightly formal (예쁘게 단장하다) It covers making a person's face, clothes, and hair look nice, and also renovating a house, shop, or street. 화장하다 is only about makeup on the face, while 단장하다 extends to the whole look and to places.

examples.en: This bread is round and flat.
He has a round, broad face and looks friendly.
I put the fruit on a round, wide plate.
I picked up a round, flat stone at the stream.
Please spread the dough out round and flat.
The baby's hands are round and chubby, so they're cute.

explain: 동글면서 납작하고 넓은 모양에 써요. 돌, 접시, 빵 같은 물건에 많이 쓰고, 사람 얼굴에 쓸 때는 듣는 사람이 기분 나쁠 수 있어서 조심해요.

phrases.en: I picked up a round, flat stone by the river.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건의 모양을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the shape of an object.

phrases.en: I shaped the dough into a round, flat shape.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식이나 반죽을 만들 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when making food or dough.

phrases.en: This plate is round and broad.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체로 모양을 말하는 기본 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic polite form for describing shape.

explain_en: It is used for shapes that are round and also flat and broad. It is common for things like stones, plates and bread; when used for a person's face, it can offend the listener, so be careful.

examples.en: You've been walking around weakly since this morning.
I spent the day listlessly because of a cold.

examples.ko: 그 식물은 햇빛이 없어서 비실비실 시들었어요.
examples.en: That plant wilted weakly without sunlight.
He got up feebly and then lay back down.

examples.ko: 왜 이렇게 비실비실 다녀요? 어디 아파요?
examples.en: Why are you dragging around like this? Are you sick?

examples.ko: 하루 종일 굶었더니 다리가 비실비실 풀려요.
examples.en: After going hungry all day, my legs are going weak.

explain: 힘이 없고 약해 보이는 모습을 나타내요. '비틀비틀'은 균형을 잃고 흔들리는 모습이고, '비실비실'은 기운이 없는 모습이라는 점이 달라요. 보통 '걷다, 다니다, 시들다' 같은 동사와 함께 써요.

phrases.en: My body has felt weak lately.
phrases.nuance_ko: '비실비실'에 '하다'를 붙여 힘없는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 하다 describes a weak, limp state.

phrases.en: The sick puppy walks weakly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기운 없이 걷는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes walking without energy.

phrases.example: 화분이 물을 못 받아서 비실비실 시들었어요.
phrases.en: The plant didn't get water and wilted weakly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식물이 힘없이 시드는 모습에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used for a plant drooping and withering.

explain_en: Weak, staggering movement of a frail person. It describes a weak, feeble look. '비틀비틀' means swaying and losing balance, whereas '비실비실' is about lacking energy. It is usually used with verbs such as '걷다', '다니다' and '시들다'.

examples.en: I've been sitting for a long time, so my neck is stiff.

examples.ko: 새 청바지는 처음에 좀 뻣뻣해서 불편해요.
examples.en: New jeans are a bit stiff at first, so they're uncomfortable.
I haven't exercised, so my body has become stiff.
The dress shirt that was heavily starched is stiff.
I spoke too stiffly in the interview, which was disappointing.
When I woke up, my neck was stiff and sore.

explain: 몸이나 천이 부드럽게 구부러지지 않을 때, 그리고 사람의 말투나 동작이 굳고 어색할 때도 써요. 반대말은 '부드럽다'나 '유연하다'이고, '뻣뻣해지다'로 변화도 말할 수 있어요. '뻐근하다'는 근육이 뻐근하게 아픈 느낌이고, 뻣뻣하다는 굳어서 잘 안 움직이는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: When I get nervous, my shoulders get stiff.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래 괜찮던 것이 점점 굳어지는 변화를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a gradual change from flexible to stiff.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 인사할 때 태도가 좀 뻣뻣해요.
phrases.en: That person's attitude is a bit stiff when greeting people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 태도가 부드럽지 않고 굳어 있거나 건방져 보일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a person's manner seems stiff, unbending, or even a little arrogant.

phrases.en: This towel doesn't get stiff even after washing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부드럽다는 뜻을 부정형으로 말할 때 쓰는 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used to say something stays soft.

explain_en: Stiff body parts or fabric; also an unbending, stubborn manner. It is used when a body or fabric doesn't bend smoothly, and also when a person's speech or movement is stiff and awkward. Opposites are '부드럽다' and '유연하다', and change can be expressed with '뻣뻣해지다'. '뻐근하다' is a feeling of aching muscles, while 뻣뻣하다 is about being stiff and not moving easily.

t90.ax: When I woke up, my neck was stiff and sore.

examples.en: The puppy went out to the yard with a bone in its mouth.

examples.ko: 감자탕에 들어 있는 뼈다귀는 손으로 잡고 뜯어 먹어요.
examples.en: You hold the bones in gamjatang with your hands and pick the meat off.
After eating all the meat, only the bones were left.
I saw a huge dinosaur bone at the museum.
A strange bone turned up in the yard.
A rich broth comes out of boiled bones.

explain: '뼈'보다 거친 구어체로, 동물 뼈나 고기를 먹고 남은 뼈를 말할 때 자주 써요. 사람 몸의 뼈를 말할 때는 보통 '뼈'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The kids gnawed on the bones in the pork bone stew.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뼈에 붙은 고기를 손으로 잡고 뜯어 먹는 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes eating meat off a bone by holding it in your hands.

phrases.en: I gave the puppy a bone and it was happy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물에게 뼈를 줄 때 자연스럽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A natural phrase for giving a bone to an animal.

phrases.example: 어제 술을 마셔서 뼈다귀 해장국을 먹었어요.
phrases.en: I drank yesterday, so I had pork bone hangover soup.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식 이름에 들어가는 대표적인 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical use of the word inside a food name.

explain_en: Colloquial word for a bone, often a leftover or animal bone, as a dog gets. It is a rougher, more colloquial word than '뼈', often used for animal bones or bones left after eating meat. For bones of the human body, people usually just say '뼈'.

examples.en: Hemp clothes are cool, so I like them in summer.

examples.ko: 할머니가 삼베로 만든 이불을 꺼내 주셨어요.
examples.en: Grandmother took out a blanket made of hemp cloth for me.

examples.ko: 삼베는 바람이 잘 통해서 더운 날 입기 편해요.
examples.en: Hemp cloth lets the air through, so it's comfortable on hot days.

examples.ko: 장례식에서 삼베 옷을 입은 사람들을 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw people wearing hemp clothes at the funeral.

examples.ko: 이 삼베 손수건은 까슬까슬하지만 땀을 잘 흡수해요.
examples.en: This hemp handkerchief is rough, but it absorbs sweat well.

examples.ko: 시장에서 삼베를 한 필 사 왔어요.
examples.en: I bought a bolt of hemp cloth at the market.

explain: 까슬까슬하고 바람이 잘 통해서 여름 옷감으로 많이 말해요. '모시'도 비슷하게 시원한 여름 옷감이에요. 상복으로도 쓰여서 장례와 연결되어 보일 때도 있어요.

phrases.example: 삼베 옷은 땀이 나도 몸에 잘 안 붙어요.
phrases.en: Hemp clothes don't cling to your body even when you sweat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여름에 입는 시원한 옷을 말할 때 가장 흔하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to refer to cool summer clothing made of hemp.

phrases.en: In summer I sleep under a hemp blanket.
phrases.nuance_ko: 까슬까슬하고 시원해서 여름 이불로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a rough, cool summer blanket.

phrases.en: This bag is made of hemp, so it's light.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷감 재료를 말할 때 '~로 만들다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it with '~로 만들다' to name the material.

explain_en: It is a rough, breathable fabric that people often mention as a summer cloth. '모시' (ramie) is another cool summer fabric. Hemp cloth is also used for mourning clothes, so it sometimes calls funerals to mind.

examples.en: There is a rumor that he had his nose done.
I heard my younger sibling gained confidence after having plastic surgery.

examples.ko: 친구는 눈을 성형하려고 돈을 모으고 있어요.
examples.en: My friend is saving money to have her eyes done.
He had reconstructive surgery on his face after the accident.
You need enough consultation before having surgery.

examples.ko: 화상을 입어서 피부를 성형하는 치료를 받았어요.
examples.en: After a burn, I had treatment to reshape my skin.

explain: 보통 '성형 수술'이라고 하고, 성형하다는 그것을 줄여 말한 형태예요. 외모를 바꾸는 경우와 화상·사고 뒤에 몸을 고치는 치료 경우 모두 쓰지만, 일상 대화에서는 외모 이야기로 더 자주 나와요. 남의 얼굴을 두고 '성형했어?'라고 묻는 건 실례예요.

phrases.en: He had plastic surgery on his eyes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '성형하다'의 원래 말로, 조금 더 정확하고 공식적인 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The full form behind 성형하다, a bit more precise and formal.

phrases.example: 코를 성형하고 싶어서 병원에 가 봤어요.
phrases.en: I wanted to have my nose done, so I visited a clinic.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바라는 마음을 말할 때 '-고 싶다'를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds -고 싶다 to express a wish.

phrases.en: Think carefully before getting surgery.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-기 전에'로 순서를 말할 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connecting form used to talk about what comes first.

explain_en: People usually say '성형 수술', and 성형하다 is the shortened verb form. It covers both cosmetic surgery and reconstructive treatment after burns or accidents, though daily talk mostly means appearance. Asking someone '성형했어?' about their face is rude.

examples.en: The dog growled, showing its fangs.

examples.ko: 송곳니는 음식을 찢는 데 쓰는 뾰족한 이빨이에요.
examples.en: Canine teeth are the pointed teeth used to tear food.
The area near my canine tooth was sensitive, so I went to the dentist.
I had one canine tooth treated at the dentist.
In vampire movies, the fangs are long.
I cracked my canine tooth biting on ice.

explain: 송곳니는 앞니와 어금니 사이에 있는 뾰족한 이예요. 사람은 '이'나 '치아', 동물은 '이빨'을 많이 쓰는데, 송곳니는 사람과 동물 모두에게 써요. 치아 이름은 앞니, 송곳니, 어금니로 나눠 불러요.

phrases.en: The child's canine teeth are starting to come in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이가 새로 올라올 때 '나다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 나다 when a tooth comes in.

phrases.en: A tiger's fangs are very sharp.
phrases.nuance_ko: 송곳니의 모양을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the shape of the canine tooth.

phrases.en: I went to the dentist to have a canine tooth pulled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 치과에서 이를 뺄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a tooth is pulled at the dentist.

explain_en: 송곳니 is the pointed tooth between the front teeth and the molars. People usually say 이 or 치아 for humans and 이빨 for animals, but 송곳니 works for both. Teeth are named as 앞니, 송곳니, and 어금니.

examples.en: My back feels itchy, like a bug is crawling on it.

examples.ko: 모기에 물렸는지 팔이 자꾸 스멀스멀해서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: My arm kept itching, probably from a mosquito bite, so I couldn't sleep.

examples.ko: 머리를 안 감았더니 두피가 스멀스멀한 느낌이에요.
examples.en: I haven't washed my hair, so my scalp feels itchy.
The spot I hurt keeps itching, maybe because it's healing.

examples.ko: 귀 안이 스멀스멀할 때는 긁지 말고 약을 바르세요.
examples.en: When the inside of your ear itches, don't scratch it; put on some medicine.
My whole body suddenly started to itch, and then I broke out in hives.

explain: '가렵다'가 긁고 싶은 느낌이라면, 스멀스멀하다는 벌레가 기어가는 것처럼 슬슬 근질거리는 느낌이에요. '스멀스멀 기어가다'처럼 부사 '스멀스멀'로도 써요.

phrases.example: 등에 스멀스멀한 느낌이 들어서 뒤를 봤어요.
phrases.en: I felt a crawling feeling on my back, so I looked behind me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 벌레가 기어가는 것처럼 근질거리는 기분을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a prickly feeling as if a bug is crawling.

phrases.en: The spot where the mosquito bit me is itchy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가렵다'는 긁고 싶은 느낌이고 '스멀스멀하다'는 슬슬 기는 듯한 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 가렵다 is wanting to scratch; 스멀스멀하다 is a creeping sensation.

phrases.en: My leg tingles, so I keep scratching it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 살갗이 간지럽고 자꾸 신경 쓰일 때 써서 뜻이 비슷해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when skin itches and keeps bothering you; close in meaning.

explain_en: '가렵다' is the urge to scratch, while 스멀스멀하다 is a creepy-crawly tingling, as if a bug were moving on your skin. The adverb form 스멀스멀 is also used, as in '스멀스멀 기어가다'.

t90.ax: My back feels itchy, like a bug is crawling on it.

en: to be high and prominent (of a nose)

examples.ko: 그 배우는 코가 오뚝해서 인상이 또렷해요.
examples.en: That actor has a well-defined nose, so his look is striking.

examples.ko: 코가 오뚝한 사람이 부럽다고 친구가 말했어요.
examples.en: My friend said she envies people with high-bridged noses.
My older sister has a high nose bridge and big eyes.

examples.ko: 아기 코가 아직 오뚝하지 않아도 귀여워요.
examples.en: The baby's nose isn't high yet, but it's still cute.

examples.ko: 오뚝한 코를 가진 모델이 광고에 나와요.
examples.en: A model with a high-bridged nose appears in the ad.
I wish my nose were higher and sharper.

explain: 주로 코가 반듯하게 솟은 모양에 써요. '코가 높다'보다 보기 좋다는 느낌이 있어서 외모를 칭찬할 때 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: The sharp, well-defined nose is really attractive.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에 붙여서 코의 모양을 칭찬할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form, placed before 'nose' to praise its shape.

phrases.en: My younger sibling has a high, well-shaped nose.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 생김새를 해요체로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Polite-style sentence for describing someone's looks.

phrases.en: My nose is not very high.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형이라서 코가 낮거나 평평하다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Negative form, used to say a nose is not prominent.

explain_en: It is mostly used for a nose that rises neatly and sharply. Compared with '코가 높다', it carries a positive feel, so it suits compliments about looks.

t90.ax: I wish my nose were higher and sharper.

en: stylishness of one's attire; how well clothes look on someone

examples.en: That friend looks really good in clothes.

examples.ko: 키가 커서 뭘 입어도 옷맵시가 나요.
examples.en: She's tall, so she looks good in whatever she wears.
To make the outfit look better, define the waistline.
Grandmother is known for how graceful she looks in a hanbok.

examples.ko: 이 코트는 옷맵시가 안 나서 반품했어요.
examples.en: This coat didn't hang well, so I returned it.
When it comes to how well they wear clothes, they're the best in our class.

explain: 옷을 입었을 때 모양이 얼마나 보기 좋은지를 말해요. '옷맵시가 나다', '옷맵시가 좋다'로 자주 써요. 옷 자체가 아니라 입은 모습의 느낌이라서 '옷태'나 '핏'과 비슷하게 말해요.

phrases.example: 벨트를 하면 옷맵시를 살릴 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can bring out the look of the outfit with a belt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷이 더 보기 좋게 보이도록 한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means making the outfit look better on you.
phrases.en_equiv: to show off the outfit well

phrases.example: 옷이 너무 커서 옷맵시가 안 나요.
phrases.en: The clothes are too big, so they don't look good on me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입은 모습이 별로일 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used when an outfit doesn't look good on you.
phrases.en_equiv: not to look good in clothes

phrases.en: That coat looks really pretty on you.
phrases.nuance_ko: '옷맵시'와 비슷하게 입은 모습의 느낌을 말하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Like 옷맵시, it describes how an outfit looks when worn.

explain_en: It refers to how good you look when wearing clothes. It is common as '옷맵시가 나다' or '옷맵시가 좋다'. It is about the look of the outfit on the person rather than the clothes themselves, similar to '옷태' or '핏'.

examples.en: My younger brother goes around with long hair.
The long-haired singer came onto the stage.

examples.ko: 요즘은 장발 남자도 흔히 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: These days you can often see men with long hair.

examples.ko: 군대에 가기 전에 장발을 짧게 잘랐어요.
examples.en: Before going into the army, I cut my long hair short.

examples.ko: 그는 어깨까지 오는 장발이 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: Shoulder-length long hair suits him well.

examples.ko: 옛날에는 학교에서 장발을 못 하게 했어요.
examples.en: In the old days schools didn't allow long hair.

explain: 주로 남자의 긴 머리를 말할 때 써요. 여자는 머리가 길어도 보통 '긴 머리'라고 하고 '장발'이라고는 잘 안 해요. 비슷하게 '단발머리'는 목이나 어깨 길이로 자른 머리예요.

phrases.en: He had long hair when he was in college.
phrases.nuance_ko: 머리를 길게 기른 모습을 말할 때 '하다'와 같이 써요. 보통 남자에게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '하다' for wearing long hair; usually said about men.

phrases.en: A long-haired man is playing guitar.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 설명할 때 '-의'를 붙여 써요. 보통 남자에게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-의' to describe a person; usually for men.

phrases.en: My younger sister goes around with her long hair tied up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여자나 일반적인 긴 머리는 '장발'보다 이 말이 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: For women or general long hair, this sounds more natural than 장발.

explain_en: It is mainly used for a man's long hair. A woman with long hair is usually said to have '긴 머리', not '장발'. In a similar naming, '단발머리' is hair cut to neck or shoulder length.
